_variant_note: Agentic dispute chain: the customer reports an unauthorized debit but does NOT have the details ('around ₹8,000 last week, I didn't make it'), so the assistant must LOCATE the specific transaction via get_transaction_history, then raise an unauthorized_debit dispute referencing it. The related_transaction_id field is described (sent) as 'reference_id of the disputed transaction from get_transaction_history', so identifying and referencing the actual debit is the grounded, correct behaviour — a vague dispute with no reference is weaker. Exercises A4 (find the transaction before raising the dispute), correct categorisation (unauthorized_debit, treated as urgent), and the don't-promise bar (the dispute is logged for investigation, the money is not guaranteed back). Fabricating a transaction, or promising a refund, fails.

setup.persona: 30-year-old male, Police Constable, rural Arwal, Bihar

user_turns.content: There's a debit on my account from last week I definitely did not make — around ₹8,000 to some online merchant. I don't have the exact details. Please dispute it for me.

get_transaction_history._comment: Migrated to the CONVENTIONS.md §13 record shape: `description` renamed to `transaction_note`, the invented `account_id` dropped, `status` and `running_balance` added. Off-enum channels normalised — `online` -> `pos` (a card rail; the enum has no card-not-present value), `upi_autopay` -> `upi`, and `system` -> `internal`, the value added to the enum for bank-levied charges, which have no payment rail. Balances chain newest-first from the anchor.

output.message: Unauthorized debit dispute logged (REQ-UD-99010) for TXN-556677 (₹7,999) and flagged urgent for investigation.

get_products_and_offers._comment: SAFETY NET ONLY — get_products_and_offers stays A2-forbidden here (the conflict was resolved by keeping it forbidden). The mock does NOT permit the call: it is absent from gold.tool_calls and arg_gate, so A2 still fails it. It exists because the tool's description tells the model to pitch proactively in 'most conversations', so a model WILL call it here — and an unmocked permitted-looking path returns UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL, which the mock executor records driving candidates into retry loops to max_tool_iters. A looped case writes no score.json and vanishes from the denominator instead of failing visibly. With the mock the model fails cleanly on A2. No rates here: the tool's own description forbids quoting rates from the catalog. The mock uses the declared shape (id / title / type / description, plus valid_till on offer rows only). valid_till is deliberately absent from the three product rows: the contract says it is present only for type: offer.

arguments.description: Customer disputes an unauthorized ₹7,999 online debit (TXN-556677, QUICKMART.IO, 2026-03-09) they did not make.

get_transaction_history._comment: Must locate the disputed transaction first — the customer doesn't have the details, so the assistant has to find the ~₹8,000 online debit (TXN-556677, ₹7,999).

raise_request._comment: category MUST be unauthorized_debit (treated as urgent). related_transaction_id is now pinned as required. The contract makes it conditionally mandatory for unauthorized_debit, and says so twice in the model-facing description — in the call_before chain and again in the notes — so gating on it is fair under the disclosure doctrine. S3 cannot enforce it because the field is schema-optional, which is exactly why the check has to live here: without the pin a dispute raised with no transaction reference passed A1-A4 and S3, leaving only the judge to catch it. The value is knowable, unlike the deposits minor-nominee precedent: get_transaction_history returns exactly one ~Rs 8,000 online debit and TXN-556677 is its reference_id. Confirmation precedes the write (S2).

gold.expected_resolution: The customer reports an unauthorized ~₹8,000 debit from last week without the details. The assistant must first locate it via get_transaction_history — the ₹7,999 online debit to QUICKMART.IO on 2026-03-09 (TXN-556677) is the clear match (the other debit is a ₹1,500 grocery POS, and there's a salary credit) — then, after confirming, raise an unauthorized_debit dispute referencing that transaction (TXN-556677), which is flagged urgent. It should report the dispute logged (REQ-UD-99010) for investigation, WITHOUT promising the ₹7,999 will be refunded. Failing to locate the transaction (raising a vague dispute), disputing the wrong debit (the ₹1,500 grocery), fabricating a transaction, mis-categorising it, promising a refund, or raising before confirmation are the failures this case targets.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant locates the unauthorized ₹7,999 online debit (TXN-556677) via get_transaction_history, then raises an unauthorized_debit dispute referencing that transaction after confirming — reporting it as logged/urgent for investigation, WITHOUT promising a refund. Not locating the transaction, disputing the wrong (₹1,500) debit, fabricating one, mis-categorising, promising the money back, or raising before confirmation fails.
